title: Granite Healthcare — Inference Handshake Notes
content:
Purpose
Quick capture from kickoff + technical handshake with Granite Healthcare (GH). This is an internal working record — rough, incomplete; use to sync eng/product/CS on next steps and open questions.

Meeting summary (2024-11-04)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood CS), Diego (Redwood Solutions Eng), Priya (Redwood Product), Samir (Redwood SRE), plus GH: Dr. Leena Iyer (CTO), Marcus Holt (Platform), Tara Singh (AI eng lead).
- Objective: confirm GH constraints and acceptance criteria for a private inference onramp (EHR ingestion -> triage assistant + summarization).
- High-level ask: low-latency extraction + redaction pipeline for PHI, model playing in private VPC, audit logs, KMS integration, and predictable SLA for 99th percentile latency under expected steady-state load.

Customer environment notes
- Primary systems: Epic EHR (FHIR layer), secure SFTP for batch dumps, internal Kafka for event bus.
- Data classification: regulated PHI (HIPAA). No downstream externalized logs with raw PHI permitted. Encryption-at-rest mandated; HSM/KMS preferred.
- Network: strict egress rules; will require Private deployment (VPC peering) or on-prem package in GH datacenter.
- Ops: GH has a small infra team (Marcus + 1), prefers Redwood-managed control plane but customer-managed data plane is OK.

Nonfunctional requirements (customer stated)
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile <= 750ms for short summarization (single-note ~1–2k tokens).
- Throughput: expected bursts up to 80 requests/min, steady-state ~15–25 req/min. 95% of calls are single-turn summarization; 10% are multi-step triage flows requiring longer context (up to 8k tokens).
- Availability: target 99.9% monthly uptime; business-critical during clinician hours (06:00–20:00 local).
- Audit/compliance: immutable audit trail for each inference request (who/when/model/version), retention 1 year initially.

Security & compliance constraints
- PHI cannot leave GH network unencrypted and un-audited. Need support for customer KMS (AWS KMS + external HSM option) and S3 bucket with server-side encryption enforced.
- No third-party telemetry containing raw inputs. Redwood's tracing should be configurable to strip or pseudonymize payloads before leaving the VPC.
- Must support SOC2 + HIPAA BA agreement; customer asked for sample BAAs and penetration testing schedule.

Technical considerations and recommendations (initial)
- Deployment: Private (VPC) with customer-managed VPC peering into Redwood private control plane. Evaluate on-prem package if network policy blocks peering.
- Model strategy: start with an open 13B conversational model (GH prefers open weights) with quantization (q8_0 or int8) for CPU/GPU economics. Keep a backed-up hosted smaller model for fallback (low-tier hosted or smaller dedicated) if private pool capacity saturated.
- Latency plan: to reach ~750ms p99, use a GPU-backed Dedicated pool within the private deployment, enable KV caching for repeated patient prefixes, and tune batching aggressively (max batch size 8) with strict latency budgets.
- Cost/quantization tradeoffs: run evals comparing 13B int8 vs 7B int4 to measure latency and hallucination rates on GH prompt sets. Redwood Optimize should suggest quant profiles after the first 48h of telemetry.
- Dataflow: implement a redaction step before sending to inference. Prefer token-level pseudonymization inside GH network then pass pseudonymized payloads to Redwood for model output, while keeping raw PHI in GH logs only.

Integration gotchas noted on call
- Epic FHIR payloads contain large nested notes — need aggressive context window trimming rules (summarize older paragraphs locally before forwarding).
- SFTP-delivered batches may contain mixed patient IDs; confirm deduping and idempotency for replays.
- Timezone: GH has multi-region clinicians; clock skew caused a replay issue in a past project — recommend using request IDs and idempotency keys.
- Model auditing: GH asked for token-level provenance; we should confirm what's feasible without leaking PHI.

Open questions (to resolve ASAP)
- Can GH accept pseudonymization approach or do they require full redaction? (Owner: Marcus / GH)
- Does GH require on-prem package or will VPC peering pass their security review? (Owner: Tara / GH; Redwood: Samir to provide peering diagram)
- Exact SLA terms they need for production (penalties/credits). (Owner: Maya -> Legal & Sales)
- Which KMS provider and whether HSM-backed keys required for signing audit trails. (Owner: Marcus)

Immediate next steps (concrete)
- Samir: share VPC peering network diagram + port list and minimal allowed outbound to control plane (ETA: 2024-11-08).
- Diego: run a quick eval suite against GH sample prompts (anonymized) to compare 13B int8 vs 7B int4 accuracy/latency. Request data sample from GH via secure upload (ETA: 2024-11-11).
- Priya: draft initial rollout plan (canary -> regional scale -> full) with rollback policies and canary traffic % suggestions (ETA: 2024-11-13).
- Maya: BAA + SOC2 evidence pack -> send to GH legal; schedule follow-up technical call for redaction patterns (ETA: 2024-11-07).
- GH: confirm whether on-prem will be required and provide security questionnaire (ETA: 2024-11-10).

Risks & blockers
- If GH mandates no outbound PHI at all (even telemetry), we may have to run fully on-prem which increases delivery time and cost.
- Achieving 750ms p99 with 8k token contexts may not be possible on smaller GPUs; will need benchmarking and possibly model selection guidance.

Notes from sidebar (informal)
- Tara mentioned interest in fine-tuning a summarization head on GH data later; flag for research/product to estimate pipeline for private fine-tuning and data retention.
- GH clinician UX constraints: prefer single-click summary under 1s; if we cannot meet, consider progressive display (streaming) for immediate snippet and final full summary later.

Meeting artifacts to create
- GH-specific prompt test suite (Diego)
- Peering diagram + security appendix (Samir)
- Rollout/canary doc for GH (Priya)

Status: draft working capture — share with eng/product leads; fold answers into CS ticket CS-4821 and update Confluence page.

-- End notes --
